last_key_points: Lebanon, not direct U.S.-Iran fire, became the primary ceasefire spoiler after heavy Israeli strikes and renewed Hezbollah rocket launches into northern Israel.
Hormuz remained permit-gated and commercially unclear through the evening, with no convincing evidence of broad tanker-flow normalization despite ceasefire headlines.
The Pakistan channel hardened from diplomatic speculation into a scheduled Saturday principals-level meeting led by Vice President JD Vance in Islamabad.
Crude retained a meaningful physical-risk premium, with Brent around 96.24 and WTI around 94.41 even after the panic phase unwound.
Late OSINT flow raised but did not verify renewed strike risk against UAE-linked energy assets and possible Israeli activity over Iran, keeping headline sensitivity high overnight.
